title: French officials blame Iran for supermarket fridge hacking
summary: The recent cyberattack on supermarkets in France was organized by Iran's Revolutionary Guards, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot has said, describing the hacking as "unprecedented."

image.caption: Stores in several countries across Europe recently experienced fridge and freezer issuesImage: Elsa Rancel/Ouest-France/PHOTOPQR/MAXPPP/IMAGO

blocks.text: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said the attacks on French supermarkets last month came from Iran, and were carried out by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), a powerful paramilitary force loyal to the Iranian regime.
"This attack is unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression," Barrot said, adding "we will implement sanctions at the European level against all those responsible for this attack."
The comparatively simple cyberattack nevertheless had dramatic consequences, spoiling large quantities of produce and in some cases setting temperatures so high that refrigeration units caught fire.
It was launched on October 11 but last week a series of similar incidents affected French supermarkets and authorities even reported a failed attempt to hack cooling units at blood banks.
